title: Book Two · Chapter 118: Mum's Afternoon
story:
Mum puts her blue skirt on the bed on Saturday. Beside it she sets a small cloth bag and a pair of clean shoes.

“I am going to see my friend after lunch,” she says.

Ronan looks at the half-finished trousers on her table.

“What about these?”

“The customer comes on Monday. I have time tomorrow morning.”

“Can you finish first?”

“I could. I am still going this afternoon.”

Dad looks up from the bread.

“A clear answer.”

Mum points at his plate. “A clear space. Please put that in the kitchen.”

Dad takes the plate. Ronan carries the cups. In the little kitchen, they stand shoulder to shoulder and cannot both turn at once.

“You first,” Dad says.

“Your legs first.”

“My legs are still attached.”

Ronan laughs and moves out of the doorway.

After lunch, Mum leaves in her clean shoes. Dad has the afternoon free. He asks Ronan to walk to the square with him.

“Can we take the bike?”

“Yes. We will check the brakes.”

Ronan is taller now. Dad moves the seat a little. He checks the seat fixings. Then he lets Ronan try the bike. The blue paint has small marks near the back wheel. The old bell still rings.

They walk through the crowded lane. At the square, Ronan rides three slow circles. Dad sits near the edge with the water bottle.

A boy with a ball asks to share the open ground. Ronan stops and talks with him. They use opposite sides. There is room if nobody races across the middle.

The ball rolls toward Ronan's wheel. Dad watches him slow down and turn away.

“That was tidy.”

“The turn?”

“The stop.”

Ronan likes the praise. He rides once more, then parks beside Dad.

“Jun plays with me sometimes,” he says.

Dad unscrews the bottle cap.

“Good.”

“He will not do a reading page with me.”

“That is his choice.”

“Everyone keeps saying that.”

Dad takes a drink, then hands over the bottle.

“It can still hurt.”

Ronan looks at him. Dad does not tell him to stop feeling sad. They sit until the ball boy calls for help with a ball under the bench.

At home, the sewing table is empty. Dad starts supper. Ronan washes vegetables in a bowl. He drops one wet leaf onto Dad's shoe.

“New decoration,” Dad says.

Mum comes home after sunset. She has a little packet of cakes from her friend. She eats one while Ronan tells her about the shared square. Dad keeps his decorated shoe on until she sees the leaf.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

attached＝连着的；opposite＝相对的；decoration＝装饰；fixings＝固定件。

## 理解问题

1. Mum为什么没有先做完所有缝补活再出门？
2. Dad怎样回应Ronan难过的感受？

## 读句子

**Ronan / washes vegetables / in a bowl.** Ronan／在盆里／洗菜。
